_what_this_is: Authored, and CANDIDATES ONLY. A script cannot say why two pages connect; these were derived from the rulings and are seeded into each page once, for a writer to keep, rewrite or delete. They are never regenerated over.

edges.clause: A region's anger is the fuel a movement grows on.
Anger raises movement share; past forty per cent the civil-war clock starts.
The four valves exist to answer the anger this page measures.

edges.evidence: DESIGN.md:491 — superlinear occupation surcharge; js/sentiment.js:139 suppression term
edges.clause: Angry ground is dearer to hold, and the bill rises faster than the map.

edges.evidence: docs/design/IDEATION-PLAN.md:35 — "Secession is not a leaf. It is the scoreboard."
edges.clause: Secession is the scoreboard, and this page is how the score is kept.

edges.evidence: DESIGN.md:1435 — "suppression costs you the people who can leave"
edges.clause: Govern badly and the people who can leave, leave.
A movement that has grown enough starts making demands of its government.
Movements past forty per cent together start the countdown to civil war.
The movement approaches you; a nation cannot simply pick one to back.
Whether a country still waits for the old union is read off its movements.
A movement that wants a union demands that you go and ask a neighbour.
Every movement is a painted patch of counties, never a state line.
A reunification movement declares a winner among claimants, not a new country.
People in a movement join its militia instead of your army.
Your money makes the movement grow faster on ground you do not hold.
Every quarter you pay is a quarter not spent on your own country.
Funding rebels inside a neighbour is one of the five roads to hostility.
Dallas can buy the argument over Texas instead of fighting it.
Petitions, offers and everything like them are diplomacy's, not secession's.
Being seen to fund somebody's rebels is remembered, and worse than recognising them.
Every nation on the board exists because of what happened here.
The game opens after the story has finished; the dice only set sizes.
The bicentenary arrives with five governments each claiming to be Texas.
Two years is eight turns, so every grudge on the board is still fresh.
What Washington lost is written into its record before the first turn.
The break-up is a chain of events, and the chain could run again.

edges.evidence: docs/design/secession-ideation.md §8, cited at events-ideation.md:7 and diplomacy-ideation.md:5
edges.clause: This is the opening chapter every other story page hangs from.
Every nation appears in every game; only its size is rolled.
The successor states are the claimants competing to restore what broke.
A nation born of a movement makes all its founding ground that movement's heartland.
Four nations are deliberately built with no movement inside them at all.

edges.evidence: Round 1 rulings 5, 6, 7 and 10, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:634 table; DESIGN.md:152
edges.clause: Each nation is a set of real counties, drawn on the real map.
Washington's armed share was set by hand at six per cent, badged an estimate.

edges.evidence: Round 1 ruling 29, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:1071 (the Gulf Compact, the Allegheny Republic)
edges.clause: The names on the map are the story's, and were chosen deliberately.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 4 cause 2 (:735) and ruling 17(d) (:1132); claimant lists at ruling 32 (:2179)
edges.clause: Two nations claiming the same inheritance are hostile, and never stop being.
A claimant may never join a union; it must win the argument first.
There can be no federation across Texas until somebody has won Texas.
The movement crowns whichever claimant already holds most of the old country.
Austin is the legitimate Texas; the other four open as rebels.
A claimant can pay to grow the movement rather than march for it.
Three eastern capitals contest the old union's seat; Boston is out.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 23, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:1649; Round 1 ruling 42, secession-ideation.md:1319
edges.clause: Govern well and provinces grow movements that want to come back.
It opens weak because everything it lost is written into its record.
The old union is one of the four things the board is fighting to restore.
Every broken promise abroad is a province that stops waiting, for good.
Does Washington open recognising nobody, and cut itself off from everyone?

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 24, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:1685; secession-ideation.md §8 inbox item 5
edges.clause: Trust in Washington collapsed and local powers filled the gap.
It plays against a clock it cannot stop, which nothing else in the game does.
The dice set how big each country starts, never whether it exists.
Growing movements roll a core that always holds and a periphery that may not.

edges.evidence: Round 1 ruling 26, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:1001 (superseding ruling 24's ring ladder at :928)
edges.clause: Setup extent comes from painted ground, not from rings around a centre.
Four or five fragments are painted per region; the dice say how many held together.
The board is rolled before you choose, so you pick knowing the sizes.
The Four Corners is settled three ways and the leftovers are rolled.
How armed each county is, is baked once at setup and never changes.
A movement lives where its counties are, and nowhere else.
A nation's founding ground resists an occupier hardest of all.

edges.evidence: Round 1 ruling 16, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:780; deferred.md #14 recorded there
edges.clause: Take somebody's heartland and you have taken the ground that fights back.
When a movement becomes a country, its country becomes its homeland.
Homelands are painted on the county map, by hand, like everything else here.

edges.evidence: Round 1 ruling 17, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:794 ("the reach stays hand-authored")
edges.clause: The ground outside a country that still wants in is what carries the story.
Ten per cent to trade with them, five to pass through — and nobody collects it.
With no government to push against or hold them down, movements grow unopposed.
No government means no treasury, no army, no elections, no foreign policy.
Stranded, then lawless, then organised, then a country — the whole life cycle.
Two movements can bring a government down together and neither inherits it.

edges.evidence: Round 1 ruling 38, docs/design/secession-ideation.md:1247 (dropping ruling 32's blanket premise)
edges.clause: Lawless ground is not uniformly hard to hold; the real data decides.
Lawless ground is the cheapest passage on the continent, and everyone routes through it.
An army base buys manpower, an air base buys attacks that land.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 31, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:2113 and the note at :2128
edges.clause: A naval base pays a nation that never fights, by improving trade through ports.
A movement demanding NORAD is now demanding something real and measurable.
Whoever holds the air bases is the nation for whom raiding is cheapest.
A poor nation can capture an air base and never really own it.
Bases are geography: a name, a branch, a county, a size.
There are no nuclear weapons, and that was decided rather than deferred.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 2, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:113; C57 at :138. NOT BUILT — see the war/trade note.
edges.clause: War prohibits trade and tears up the deals you had already signed.
War is the state in which you are allowed to attack at all.
A war ends only when both sides agree, and refusing is allowed.
What the war cost you is what sets the bill you may present.
A decade of fighting is paid for at home, and only peace repays it.
Ground you win is yours at once, but only under an occupier's flag.
You may declare straight from peace; the ladder is a cost, not a gate.
Declare against the federation's wishes and you leave it the same day.
A region under attack produces nothing that quarter, win or lose.
Every acre you win arrives flagged as occupied until you make peace.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 24 and its finding, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1723 and :1736
edges.clause: One action a turn already means one attack a turn, cooldown or not.
Some ground is dear to hold whoever holds it, and that never changes hands.

edges.evidence: DESIGN.md:370 — authority is cut by territory lost, occupation and overreach
edges.clause: Wars won firm your grip; overreach loosens it.

edges.evidence: js/civilwar.js:4-7 — triggered by an annexation flipping the plurality, GDP or population
edges.clause: Bite off more than you are and your own country comes apart.
What you spent taking ground is the basis for what you may demand back.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 17, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:1371 (the default on recent conquest)
edges.clause: A neighbour fresh from taking ground is frightening, and frightening cools a yes.

edges.evidence: DESIGN.md:491-493 — superlinear surcharge, treasury into deficit near 110 occupied Areas
edges.clause: Held ground costs more the more of it you hold, and the curve bends upward.
Ground held while the war runs raises unrest and hurts the economy badly.
Your allies will not route cargo across ground you are still fighting over.
The treaty is the title deed; without it the ground stays under a soldier's flag.
Ground that resists being governed is no harder to take and far dearer to keep.
The front line is the pale part of your own country on the map.
A country that governs by garrison has announced it cannot govern otherwise.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 26, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1818 (and C109 confirmed by ruling 41)
edges.clause: Conquered people become yours only if life here is better than life there.
How hard a place is to govern is a fact about the place, not about you.
An armed county governed by people it agrees with is quiet.
Capacity is how many people here are armed, spread by how rural they are.
It is painted everywhere, heaviest on the six lawless regions.
Lawless ground turned out slightly less armed than everywhere else, not more.
An armed population is who a militia is made of.
The armed share is the ceiling on what anybody here can put in the field.

edges.evidence: docs/design/IDEATION-PLAN.md:89 — "a civil war that goes badly makes new nations"
edges.clause: A civil war that goes badly enough puts new countries on the board.
Ground cut off by a civil war and too small to stand goes lawless.
The bigger a movement grows, the more of its people arm for it instead of you.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 7, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:576 (Oregon worked at 26/26: 8,202 against 8,886)
edges.clause: A country half organised against itself fields half an army.
Today the only thing that starts one is taking too much at once.
Past forty per cent the clock runs, and a government may simply give in.
A region nobody won goes ungoverned, and its edges pick a neighbour instead.
Each state is a short list of what you may not do, and trade is on it.
Any state can become war by one nation deciding it has.
Hostility cools on a clock into wary, and wary into peace.
A cease-fire has a fixed term and three ways out of it.
A treaty runs its term and then quietly becomes peace again.
You cannot ally with somebody you are hostile toward, nor fight an ally.
A hostile neighbour cannot say yes; a wary one says yes less often.
Inside a federation everybody is at peace, so the permanent quarrels must stay outside.
Deals already signed run their term; no new deal may be signed.
What they charge to carry your goods goes up, and so does what they will accept.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 9 item 3 (:873), switched off at Wary by ruling 40 (:2561)
edges.clause: Their movement grows faster inside you — and stops dead when the quarrel cools.
Checked before anything else: a hostile nation cannot agree to join you.
There is no treaty out of hostility — only time, or a war.
Hostility is where most of the board lives, and where wars are declared from.
Guarding a hostile border costs money every quarter, forever.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 17(d) (:1132), claimants named by ruling 32 (:2179) — 33 permanent pairs
edges.clause: Thirty-three pairs of claimants are hostile on turn one and never cool.
Both sides table terms blind before it ends; the defender chooses first.
All the costs of war, and you may not attack.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 8, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:832 and the restatement at :2321
edges.clause: Nothing signed by the deadline and you fall back to hostile, not to war.
It is a waiting room that charges you war prices while you wait.
It is the only door out of a war, and both sides must open it.
Putting terms on the table is free; ending a war is cheaper than starting one.
Terms are written blind, so what you can see of them decides everything.
Signing is what turns ground you are standing on into ground you own.
Repayment is capped against what the war cost whoever sent the terms.
Break one and every neighbour but your allies turns hostile at once.
Allies are the one exception; friendship insulates you from your own bad faith.
When its term runs out the pair simply goes back to peace.
Refusing terms is allowed, and a war can run on because somebody said no.
A federation makes peace as one; a member wanting out must leave first.
The first place the game punishes you for misreading a person, not a number.
You inherit your ally's enemies — one hop only, and it cools fastest.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 27 and C110, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1892 and :1917
edges.clause: Soldiers lent to a friend are soldiers not holding your own border.
You cannot be at war with an ally, and never have to join theirs.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 27 and C111, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1892 and :1929
edges.clause: You may open a second front only if you border their enemy.
Allies do not turn on you when you break somebody else's treaty.
Subjects, protectorates and guarantees were all handed forward, not built.
An alliance is two states; a federation is many, and that is the whole difference.
A small neighbour of your enemy is worth more than a giant on the far coast.
The only demand your government cannot satisfy alone — somebody else must say yes.
Making the proposal spends your one action for the quarter.
"Let us think about it" grows the same movement inside their country.
Size, authority and influence together are what make you frightening to join.
The claimants to a broken country may never join one.
A union is one state; a federation is a union of states. Different wants.
A yes makes two countries one, and everybody in it a full member.
Whether a government may propose with nobody demanding it is still open.
A flat ten per cent replaces every deal members had with each other.
Inside a federation you are at peace with every member. Full stop.
An attack on the smallest member is a war with all of them.
Letting another country lead you costs authority and buys influence.
The elected leader gets a second, deliberately short turn of its own.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 31, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:1976 and ruling 33 at :2075
edges.clause: At most one claimant may be in any federation, so the first to build locks the rest out.
It is the answer to a union you are forbidden to give.
The gate-holders earn most and lose most, and the map decides which.
Answering a movement is free; doing what it asked costs your action.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 11a, docs/design/politics-ideation.md:986; Round 1 ruling 40, secession-ideation.md:1289
edges.clause: Each valve removes a want — and only the want that matches it.
A government that suspends an election has announced it cannot win one.
Martial law buys quiet with liberties, at several times a garrison's rate.
Lose the referendum and the region leaves cleanly, a country from day one.
Become one movement and every county that prefers another walks out.
The one concession that is an attempt rather than an act, and can fail.
Changing course is priced by how far your party has to move.
Every demand must be answered before the quarter can move at all.
Say no and it grows; string it along and it stops wanting what it wanted.
Two of the six wants are your own people demanding you take somebody's ground.
The demand names a neighbour, and asking that neighbour discharges it.
When a strung-along movement gives up, its country stops waiting for ever.
Five moves answer every demand the game can make of you.
A movement can demand a named base, and now that demand means something.
Refusing feeds the anger that runs the clock you cannot see.

edges.evidence: js/sentiment.js:74-76 — "A weak nation" and "Weak authority" are grievance terms
edges.clause: A government with a loose grip is itself a reason to organise against it.
The country that is winning is the one that finds unions hardest to get.
A little authority every quarter is the rent on somebody else leading you.
Authority reads recent losses, so the remnant opens weak without a special rule.
A new country's fervour holds its regions for four turns, then costs more than it gave.
Every valve you pull is authority spent, and the bill compounds.
A country that hands its foreign policy away has said something about itself.
Wars won firm the grip; ground lost and overreach loosen it.
A movement travels through a politics, and the wrong politics stops it dead.
An ideology is a place on the board and cannot move; a party can.
The distance a party has to travel is what changing course costs.
People move toward people who think as they do, and the map sorts itself.

edges.evidence: js/sentiment.js:4 — base = affinity(area's leading ideology, movement's ideology)
edges.clause: Anger only becomes a movement where the politics already fit.
Joining people unlike you is expensive at home, however profitable abroad.
Willingness to resist is the distance between the governed and the governors.

edges.evidence: js/civilwar.js:4 — "the annexation flips the nation's PLURALITY party"
edges.clause: Swallow enough of somebody else and their politics take your parliament.
One action a quarter already means one attack a quarter.
Doing what a movement asked is the whole of that quarter's work.
Proposing a union costs the action, by precedent rather than by new rule.
The one decision that is free and guaranteed every quarter — a precedent on purpose.
The federation's leader spends a second turn, and only on three things.
Putting peace terms on the table costs nothing at all.
Recognising a country is a signature, not a war, so it does not end the quarter.
Six whole systems are competing for one decision a quarter.
Secession is the scoreboard: nine pressures from every other system, added up.
Every movement is a verb, an adjective and a politics it travels through.
This is where new countries come from, at setup and in play.
A movement is what people want; politics is how they get it.

edges.evidence: docs/design/IDEATION-PLAN.md:70-72 (the seam rule: Unite belongs to conquest)
edges.clause: Merging with a neighbour can shatter you, so that seam belongs to war.
The first thing here a player does to somebody else rather than suffers.
Everything here is bound to painted counties, never to a state line.
The dice at setup are what make two games of this different.

edges.evidence: js/military.js:1-36 — force is one number pointed three ways
edges.clause: One pool of force, pointed at home, at the border, or at the attack.

edges.evidence: js/military.js:33-36 — "an army you keep is an army you pay for"
edges.clause: An army you keep is an army you pay for, every quarter.
How much you pointed forward is most of how a fight resolves.
Soldiers standing on a region hold it down and make the next movement.
Martial law multiplies a garrison you already have; with none, it does nothing.
Three kinds of base, each a permanent bonus sitting on real ground.

edges.evidence: js/sentiment.js:132 — a garrison buys quiet now and the grievance that feeds the next movement
edges.clause: A garrison buys quiet now and sells you the next decade.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 27 and C110, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1892 and :1917
edges.clause: What you lend a friend is a fourth slice of the same pie.
Self-rule, release and changing course are the prices a government can pay.
How freely people may disagree, and how firmly you hold your ground.
Three axes, ten positions, authoritarians at both outer ends.
A country thinly angry everywhere tears itself apart without a border moving.
How firmly a state holds itself is a political fact before a military one.
The one wholly new object this round asked for, and it is political.
Merging with a neighbour is your own people making you go and ask.
Ground with people on it and no government is a political object, not a gap.

edges.evidence: docs/design/IDEATION-PLAN.md:26 — "How well its people are fed, treated and paid"
edges.clause: The deepest of the nine pressures: how well people are fed and paid.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 4, cause 3, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:735 and the gap note at :756-761
edges.clause: Gouge a desperate neighbour and you have a quarrel — once desperation can bite.
A federation of neighbours who ignore each other is broke.

edges.evidence: js/military.js:18-22 — equipment from wealth per head
edges.clause: What your people are worth is what your soldiers are equipped with.
Lawless ground is the cheapest road on the continent because nobody rules it.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 2 (:113) vs js/moves.js:549 and js/recognition.js:377 — no war state exists in the build
edges.clause: War is ruled to prohibit trade; today only recognition can stop a deal.
Run short of something and your own people start demanding you take it.
Nothing bad happens yet to a country that does not trade at all.
A trade agreement is a signature, and both sides must admit the other exists.
How an offer is made, held open and withdrawn belongs here.
Alliances were taken thin on purpose; vassals and guarantees wait here.
Eight named states is the whole of what two countries can be to each other.

edges.evidence: Round 2 ruling 21, docs/design/conquest-ideation.md:1504 and the blocking note at :680
edges.clause: Nothing yet lets a hostile pair thaw faster, and thirty-three of them start that way.
A brand-new country that nobody will talk to is this round's whole reason.
If Washington recognises nobody, the trade block cuts it off from everyone.
A union proposed by a government nobody asked for is diplomacy's question.
The break-up was a chain of events, and the same chain could run again.
A world shock hits every country at once, and the economy has to price it.
A neighbour comes apart and the people who arrive bring their politics.
Protests at the capital: concede, crush, or wait.
The canal, the bicentenary, the year the union dissolved — nowhere yet to say any of it.
Designed last on purpose: you cannot design a shock before the thing it shocks.
Everything that moves, moves along the county map and pays for the crossing.
You can only attack what you can reach, which is what makes the map matter.

edges.evidence: js/sentiment.js:9 — pull = tanh of the sum of neighbours' shares
edges.clause: Whose neighbours have already turned is one of the nine pressures.
3,143 counties collapse to 1,676 areas, and everything is painted on them.
The toll goes to whoever's ground is crossed, so geography collects it.
People move to the areas next door, so distance is real without measuring it.
A base is a county, and the county folds into the area it belongs to.
Sixty-one countries are drawn on the same real map, county by county.
Membership is people, so a movement shrinks with whoever leaves.
Manpower comes from population, so a shrinking country fields less.
A divided country sorts itself into halves that agree with themselves.
Quality of life and liberties are the first two things a region counts against you.
The same people are the army or the militia, never both.
How armed a place is, is a share of how many people live there.
Over five hundred thousand it is a country; under it, lawless ground.
Output per head falls as people arrive, which is what stops everyone piling in.
A movement only grows where the local politics already fit it.
The same county is quiet under people it agrees with and dear under strangers.
An ideology is a location, so it is the one thing that cannot move.
Agreement is one of the four things pulling people across the map.
Self-rule buys off an autonomist movement and buys nothing from a religious one.
Political closeness is what warms a neighbour toward saying yes.
Joining people unlike you costs authority in proportion to the distance.
The board and the ideologies are fixed; wanting to change one is Aaron's call.
One action per country, and taking it ends your quarter.
Sealed peace terms are a coin toss unless you can see what you are bidding against.

edges.evidence: Round 3 ruling 17 and the deferral at docs/design/politics-ideation.md:2296-2302
edges.clause: Can you read a neighbour before you propose? Deferred, deliberately, to the design stage.
You choose your country knowing exactly how big the dice made it.

edges.evidence: CLAUDE.md, Addendum A rules — "Economy mode is a sandbox with no win condition, and testers are told so"
edges.clause: Economy mode is a sandbox with no way to win, and it says so up front.
The one decision you always get, free, before you spend the quarter.
Every system has to answer what you do about it, on a Tuesday, with one action.
Texas declared in 2034 and set its own bicentenary as the deadline.
Sixty-one countries, each with a name somebody chose and a reason for it.
Oil stopped, shortages spread, trust collapsed — a chain that could run again.
Every question round five opens came out of the story first.
Trust in Washington collapsed and local powers stepped into the gap.
The anniversary arrives with five governments each claiming to be Texas.
NORAD and Pearl Harbor were named for flavour; now they are real objects.
